update_channel_protocol.title: Update Channel Protocol
update_channel_protocol.description: The transport protocol used to deliver configuration updates to managed components. Covers both application-layer and transport-layer protocol identity.

mutual_tls_enforced.title: Mutual TLS Enforced
mutual_tls_enforced.description: Whether mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication is enforced for the configuration update channel, ensuring both client and server authenticate each other.

payload_integrity_verification.title: Payload Integrity Verification
payload_integrity_verification.description: Whether configuration update payloads are cryptographically signed and the signature is verified before application, independent of transport-layer encryption.

tls_enabled.title: TLS Enabled on Update Channel
tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS is enabled at all on the update/management channel between controller and managed components.

client_certificate_authentication_requir.title: Client Certificate Authentication Required
client_certificate_authentication_requir.description: Whether the update channel requires clients to present a valid certificate (mutual TLS) rather than using server-only TLS.

client_ca_certificate_configured.title: Client CA Certificate Configured
client_ca_certificate_configured.description: Whether a trusted CA certificate is configured for validating client certificates on the update channel, which is required for mTLS to be effective.

minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
minimum_tls_version.description: The minimum TLS protocol version negotiated or accepted by the component for update channel communications.

allowed_cipher_suites.title: Allowed TLS Cipher Suites
allowed_cipher_suites.description: List of cipher suites configured or negotiated for the update channel. Weak entries include RC4, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT, anon, MD5-signed, or DES variants.

replay_protection_mechanism.title: Replay Protection Mechanism
replay_protection_mechanism.description: Indicates what per-message replay protection is applied to configuration update messages (nonces, timestamps, sequence numbers, or none).

message_integrity_verification_enabled.title: Message Integrity Verification Enabled
message_integrity_verification_enabled.description: Whether configuration update messages are cryptographically signed or MACed so that replayed or tampered messages can be detected and rejected by recipients.

update_deduplication_enforced.title: Update Deduplication Enforced
update_deduplication_enforced.description: Whether the receiving component maintains state (e.g., a seen-nonces cache or last-applied sequence number) that prevents processing of duplicate or out-of-order configuration update messages.

payload_integrity_mechanism.title: Payload Integrity Mechanism
payload_integrity_mechanism.description: The message-layer integrity mechanism applied to configuration update payloads, independent of transport security.

transport_tls_enforced.title: Transport TLS Enforced
transport_tls_enforced.description: Whether TLS is enforced for the configuration update channel, providing the only layer of integrity protection when payload signing is absent. Cannot be downgraded.

bgp_route_filtering_enabled.title: BGP Route Filtering Enabled
bgp_route_filtering_enabled.description: Whether BGP prefix filters or route policies are configured to prevent acceptance of more-specific route advertisements that could redirect update traffic to unauthorized destinations.

update_server_ip_allowlist_enforced.title: Update Server IP Allowlist Enforced
update_server_ip_allowlist_enforced.description: Whether managed components restrict update connections to a statically defined allowlist of permitted source/destination IP addresses, preventing rogue distribution points from being reached even if routing is manipulated.

rate_limiting_enabled.title: Rate Limiting Enabled on Update Channel
rate_limiting_enabled.description: Indicates whether request-rate or bandwidth controls are enforced on the configuration update channel to prevent flooding attacks.

connection_limit_configured.title: Connection Limit Configured
connection_limit_configured.description: Indicates whether a maximum concurrent connection or request concurrency limit is configured for the update channel, providing a secondary flood-prevention control.

ca_chain_validation_enforced.title: CA Chain Validation Enforced
ca_chain_validation_enforced.description: Indicates whether the managed component enforces full certificate chain-of-trust validation when connecting to the management controller, rejecting self-signed or untrusted-CA certificates.

certificate_expiry_validation_enforced.title: Certificate Expiry Validation Enforced
certificate_expiry_validation_enforced.description: Indicates whether the managed component rejects expired certificates presented by the management controller during TLS handshake.

pinned_certificate_or_ca_configured.title: Pinned Certificate or CA Configured
pinned_certificate_or_ca_configured.description: Indicates whether the managed component pins the management controller's certificate or a specific CA, preventing substitution with a lookalike certificate from an attacker-controlled server.

network_segment_type.title: Network Segment Type
network_segment_type.description: Classification of the network segment over which configuration update traffic traverses — dedicated out-of-band management, VPN-encapsulated, flat/shared, or untrusted public network.

transport_encryption_enabled.title: Transport Encryption Enabled
transport_encryption_enabled.description: Whether the configuration update channel enforces transport-layer encryption (e.g., TLS 1.2+, IPsec) for all update traffic, protecting against interception on shared segments.

mutual_authentication_enforced.title: Mutual Authentication Enforced
mutual_authentication_enforced.description: Whether both the update source and the managed component mutually authenticate before exchanging configuration update data, preventing injection from unauthorized sources.

protocol_supports_sni_or_plaintext_heade.title: Protocol Exposes Plaintext Metadata Headers
protocol_supports_sni_or_plaintext_heade.description: Indicates whether the update protocol uses mechanisms that expose unencrypted metadata to passive observers, such as TLS SNI, unencrypted HTTP Host headers, SNMP community strings, or unencrypted MQTT topic names — even when the payload itself is encrypted.

encrypted_client_hello_enabled.title: Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) Enabled
encrypted_client_hello_enabled.description: Indicates whether TLS Encrypted Client Hello is configured to prevent SNI-based identity leakage to passive observers. When false or absent for TLS-based update channels, the server identity is revealed in plaintext.

update_channel_exposure.title: Update Channel Network Exposure
update_channel_exposure.description: The network accessibility of the configuration update channel, indicating the potential attacker population and risk surface. Used by rate-limiting and mTLS rules.
